BILL NUMBER:  S1633

 TITLE OF BILL :

An act to amend the election law, in relation to the residential
classification of certain incarcerated persons

 PURPOSE :

This legislation would direct the State Board of Elections to obtain
residential data on incarcerated persons and would require that
residential data to be used in creating Congressional, Assembly,
Senate and County Legislative Districts.

 SUMMARY OF PROVISIONS :

Section 1: Legislative Findings

Section 2: Amends the election law by adding a new section 3-112
creating the Prisoner Census Adjustment. This section would require
state agencies and local governments that operate facilities for
incarcerated individuals, including mental health facilities, as well
as other private facilities that may incarcerate persons convicted of
a criminal offense to submit a report to the State Board of Elections
containing the following information:

1. The name each person incarcerated in a facility operated by the
state agency, governmental entity, or in a private facility on behalf
of the state agency or governmental entity on the date for which the
census reports population, who completed a census form, responded to a
census inquiry or was included in any report to census officials if
such information indicated that the person resided at the facility on
that date.

2. The age, sex and race of each person included in the report.

3. The last address at which the person resided before the person's
current incarceration.  The State Board of Election would then collect
such data and prepare and disseminate adjusted populations counts for
each geographic unit included in the census counts no later than the
next September first following the date on which population counts are
released for New York State by the Bureau of the Census. The
Legislative Task Force on Demographic Research and Reapportionment
would be required to utilize the information compiled by the Board of
Elections in the creation of Congressional, Assembly, Senate and
County Legislative Districts.

Section 3: Effective Date

 JUSTIFICATION :

Article II, Section 4 of the New York State Constitution states that
"no person shall be deemed to have gained or lost a residence...
while confined to any public prison." Under this clause, the current
practice of classifying incarcerated persons as residents of their
place of incarceration, rather than residents of their place of
residence prior to incarceration, is in fact unconstitutional. The
current procedures of the U.S. Census Bureau make it difficult for the
Board of Elections and the Legislative Task Force on Demographic
Research and Reapportionment to adhere to this section of the State
Constitution. Current census records used by the Board of Elections
and the "Task Force" count incarcerated persons as residents of the
facility in which they are incarcerated.

This bill seeks to solve this problem and to bring current census
practices in New York State back in line with the State Constitution.
It does so by requiring the State Board of Elections to prepare and
disseminate adjusted population counts based on information from
government agencies and incarceration facilities for each geographic
unit included in the census counts.  Those adjusted population counts
will reflect the residence of incarcerated persons as their last
residence prior to incarceration.  All such information provided by
the Board of Elections must be utilized by the "Task Force" in the
drawing of any district boundaries.

 LEGISLATIVE HISTORY :

2008 - Referred to Elections
2007 - Referred to Elections

 FISCAL IMPLICATIONS :

Minimal administrative costs to be determined.

 EFFECTIVE DATE :
This act shall take effect immediately.

summary: Directs the state board of elections to obtain residential data on incarcerated persons to be used in creating congressional, senate, assembly, and county legislative body districts on the basis of their residence prior to incarceration, as required by law.
